deepdive.sec: Aerospace & defence — build-to-print electrical/wiring systems & high-reliability EMS (wire harnesses, panels, interconnect)

bull_bear.body: Maiden dividend announced (quantum not specified on call). Planned QIP to raise ~7–10% (sized off market cap, 5% up/down band) — proceeds for (1) capacity expansion/facility footprint, (2) operational/quality/testing infrastructure, (3) working capital for scale & long-lead inventory; seeking "the right investor." Debt has risen with growth; multi-banking framework; additional working-capital facilities secured in Q4. Inventory-coverage reduction (7.67→4 months target) is the key self-funding lever. CFO acknowledged operating cash flow still negative, improvement expected over coming years.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Margins running below the 17–22% guide; recovery hinges on qualifications converting to repeat volume.
- Negative operating cash flow and rising debt while scaling ~90%/yr — heavy working-capital intensity.
- Execution-dilutive QIP (7–10% dilution) and dependence on raising capital to fund growth.
- Customer concentration: Boeing in A&D, single large customer in each of space (Amazon) and semiconductor today.
- Legacy loss-making Boeing program (~INR70cr) still to run off in H1 FY27.
- Revenue 98% export / ~80% North America → FX, US tariff/policy and freight exposure (though customers pay freight, air-freighted, mostly CIF/customer-paid).
- Guidance is qualitative ("similar to last year"); space/semi 300–400% growth off a small base; commercial-aero entry still pre-RFP.
- Margin pressure if semiconductor volume mix dilutes blended profitability.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Very bullish and promotional — "strongest quarter in history," "structurally higher growth trajectory," "sky's the limit," "designed to compound." MD candid on margin miss (attributes to investment/qualification, promises recovery) and forthcoming on QIP, dividend, and content-share ambitions. Repeatedly deferred specific numbers (PAT margin, MRO TAM, order sizes) and invited analysts to factory visits. Confident, partnership-led narrative around Fortune/global customers and Boeing endorsement (level-loading schedules).
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- Strategic agreements (~INR3,000cr) are OVER AND ABOVE the INR715cr confirmed POs — large under-appreciated visibility layer.
- Space customer is now Amazon (Kuiper), explicitly NOT Blue Origin anymore — a customer swap.
- New semiconductor customer being onboarded is "one of the largest semiconductor manufacturers in the world" (contract imminent) — second major semi anchor.
- Commercial aerospace: OEMs building India supply base have shortlisted Rossell; RFPs expected ~Q2 FY27 — order sizes "much larger" than defence/space/semi; potentially "transformational."
- Phase-2 (2028–29): move up value chain from harnesses/panels to electromechanical integrated systems & assemblies → margin 21–30%; content per platform "X into 3 to 5."
- Capex strategy reversed: leasing 210k sq ft instead of building — faster, capital-light.
- EPA clauses, advance payments and back-to-back supplier contracts newly built into agreements to de-risk RM/working capital.
- US RTI subsidiary being pushed by a space customer to expand — could anchor US space scale-up.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

bull_bear.body:
- Proposed QIP of up to ₹300 Cr to fund strategic expansion, capacity creation and a stronger balance sheet.
- Strengthened liquidity through an additional ₹75 Cr working capital facility to support growth and larger program execution.
- Management states a philosophy of balancing growth with financial discipline while maintaining a strong and resilient balance sheet, supported by treasury and cash-flow management.
- Scale is expected to deliver stronger economics — higher margins, better asset turns and compounding returns — as the platform builds out.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Aerospace & defence (core, build-to-print wire harnesses/panels for Boeing & US military platforms; on "nearly every US military platform"; long-term 5-yr contracts with back-to-back supplier agreements). Semiconductor (wire harnesses for semicap equipment; qualified Q2 FY26, ramped immediately; new global top-tier semi customer being onboarded; ~50/50 weighting with space inside the non-A&D bucket). Commercial aerospace (currently Tier-2; shortlisted by OEMs re-shoring supply base to India; RFPs expected ~Q2 FY27; "transformational" optionality). MRO/aftermarket (DPL + AS9110 licenses now in place; marketing to existing + new customers, organic + inorganic; revenue pickup in coming quarters).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Presented as a globally recognised manufacturer of electrical wire harnesses and interconnect systems (EWIS) with a Fortune 500 client base, grown from a single customer at inception in 2011 to 30+ marquee customers across sectors.
- Moat framed as qualification and execution barriers — ITAR, AS9100D and NADCAP across 40 processes with multi-year qualification cycles — plus 8-12 year global OEM partnerships that the deck argues a new entrant cannot replicate.
- Claims deep embedding in decade-long global defence programs where switching costs are extremely high once a supplier is qualified.
- Growth is characterised as structural rather than cyclical, driven by defence budgets, commercial aerospace ramp-up, the global semiconductor mission and space liberalisation across four high-barrier industries.
- Customer validation is evidenced by Boeing Supplier of the Year (2015, 2019) and Performance Excellence awards, Honeywell Supplier Excellence (2023, 2024) and a BAE Systems Special Recognition Award (2025).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demerger] Demerged from Rossell India Ltd and relisted as Rossell Techsys Ltd in December 2024; a Rossell India senior finance executive continues on the board as a non-executive director.
- [Board] Board includes former HAL Chairman & MD Talari Suvarna Raju and former Secretary (Defense Finance) Shobhana Joshi, giving direct defence-procurement and policy access alongside promoter directors Harsh Mohan Gupta and Rishab Mohan Gupta.
- [Certification] ITAR certification and a pending CMMC V2.0 push are regulatory prerequisites for US defence work and effectively gate the addressable customer set.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: FY26 EBITDA ~13.6% (INR66cr on INR485cr), below mgmt's 17–22% structural band and sequentially weaker — repeatedly questioned by analysts. Cause: front-loaded investment in people, infrastructure, training, tooling, automation, and heavy first-article-inspection (FAI)/qualification spend for new space & semiconductor customers that generates no current-year revenue but drives repeat orders and higher margins later. Mgmt insists margins improve in FY27 and that semiconductor (despite high-volume) stays in the 17–22% band via automation. Back-to-back supplier contracts + EPA (equitable price adjustment) clauses + advance/upfront payments on long-lead single-source items mitigate raw-material and working-capital risk.
latest_quarter.title: Margins

latest_quarter.body:
First tracked file for ROSSTECH (no prior summary in repo). Key Q4 FY26 / FY26 markers from this call:
- Record Q4 revenue ~INR142cr (+62% YoY); FY26 revenue INR485cr (+87% YoY); PBT INR10cr→INR28cr; EBITDA INR38cr→INR66cr.
- FY26 EBITDA margin ~13.6% — below 17–22% structural guide and sequentially weaker; attributed to qualification/FAI and investment spend.
- Confirmed POs ~INR715cr; strategic agreements ~INR3,000cr clarified as OVER AND ABOVE POs; FY26 bids ~INR4,500cr.
- New disclosures: ~INR400cr multi-year space win; T-7 ~US$200m; space customer is Amazon (not Blue Origin); new top-tier semiconductor customer being onboarded; semi+space each guided +300–400% FY27.
- Capex pivot: leasing ~210,000 sq ft adjacent facility instead of building new.
- Capital actions: maiden dividend declared; QIP planned (~7–10% dilution); inventory coverage 10→7.67 months, targeting 4; employee cost 15.5% of revenue.
- New markets/licenses: DPL + AS9110 MRO licenses obtained; commercial-aero RFPs expected ~Q2 FY27; US RTI expansion under evaluation.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- FY27 revenue: another "similar" ~80–90% growth (vs +87% in FY26); mgmt declined a hard number. Prior 2-yr aspiration of ~INR1,300cr top line reiterated (FY26 did ~INR500cr; FY27 implicitly heading toward ~INR800cr+).
- FY27 revenue mix: ~50% aerospace & defence / ~50% non-A&D (space + semiconductor).
- Space + semiconductor each guided +300–400% YoY in FY27 (base: ~20% of FY26 revenue came from these two combined).
- EBITDA margin: structural 17–22% in current competencies; FY27 expected to improve vs FY26; MRO higher (services); phase-2 electromechanical assemblies (2028–29) could reach 21–30%.
- Semiconductor revenue potential ~US$200m in 3–5 years; T-7 strategic agreement ~US$200m.
- Inventory coverage targeted down from 7.67 months toward an eventual 4 months.
- Employee cost targeted below 15.5% of revenue.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body:
- Confirmed POs ~INR715cr; FY26 order inflow ~INR570cr.
- Strategic agreements ~INR3,000cr — OVER AND ABOVE the INR715cr POs (mgmt explicitly confirmed). POs are placed against these 6–12 months before delivery; gives ~3-year visibility.
- Bids submitted during FY26 ~INR4,500cr across aerospace/defence/space/semiconductor.
- Landmark multi-year space contract ~INR400cr won during the year; repeat orders from overseas defence customers.
- T-7 (Boeing) strategic agreement ~US$200m; deliveries started, ramp from later FY27 (mgmt suggested Q2/Q3), then 5–7 years of growth.
- Confirmed-PO split ~50/50 A&D vs non-A&D; strategic agreements skew toward A&D.
- Legacy loss-making Boeing program: ~INR75cr executed in FY26, ~INR70cr remaining (front-loaded into H1 FY27).
outlook.title: Order book

outlook.body: Macro tailwinds: global commercial-aero production ramp, rising defence GDP spend, LEO/space ecosystem build-out, semiconductor-equipment capex with China+1 supply-base diversification into India, and supply-chain-resilience demand for "trusted manufacturing partners." Company-specific: high qualification barriers (moat), 300–400% growth in space & semi, content-share expansion ("X into 3 to 5") on existing platforms (phase-2, 2028+), commercial aerospace entry, MRO, and RTI US expansion. 98% of revenue exported (~80% North America; diversifying into Southeast Asia, Middle East, Europe).
outlook.title: Growth

deepdive.thesis: Niche build-to-print wire-harness/interconnect EMS supplier on "nearly every US military platform" that just nearly doubled revenue (FY26 INR485cr, +87%) and more-than-doubled PBT, while diversifying decisively beyond aerospace/defence into space (Amazon) and semiconductor-equipment harnesses. Visibility is unusually strong: ~INR715cr confirmed POs plus ~INR3,000cr of strategic agreements on top, with mgmt guiding to another ~80–90% revenue growth in FY27 and 17–22% EBITDA margins. Multiple optionalities (commercial aerospace entry, MRO licensing, US RTI build-out, content-share gains per platform) sit outside current numbers, funded by a planned QIP (7–10% dilution).

open.item: Bids of around INR 700 crores were submitted during Q3 FY26 across aerospace, semiconductor and space, with decisions expected 6 to 12 months after submission.
Preparations for CMMC 2.0 compliance are underway targeting November 2026, alongside a DSIR licence renewed through March 2027.

Management flagged that heavy qualification/first-article-inspection spend, training and infrastructure investment depressed FY26 margins, and that rising debt/working capital needs accompany the high-growth plan, with raw-material escalation only partly passed through (some customers reject EPA clauses).
Employee cost was 15.5% of revenue in FY26 and management expects good improvement in this ratio in FY27 as scale increases.
Blended margins in current competencies to stay in the 17% to 22% band, with a definite improvement in EBITDA and PBT margin in FY27 versus FY26.
Space and semiconductor segments together to grow 300% to 400% in FY27 over FY26 (these two were ~20% of FY26 revenue).
FY27 revenue mix guided at 50% aerospace and defence and 50% non-aerospace and defence.
Roughly Rs 70 crore of the loss-making Boeing order remains to be executed in FY27, weighted to the first two quarters, after Rs 75 crore executed in FY26.

Leasing an additional ~210,000 sq ft facility near existing operations (instead of building new) to which space and semiconductor programs will migrate, expected to deliver revenue comparable to the existing facility.
Company is pursuing a QIP this financial year targeting dilution of about 7% to 10%, with proceeds for capacity expansion, operational infrastructure and working capital.
Management guided FY27 revenue growth at similar levels to FY26's 87% growth (analyst framed it as 80-90%, confirmed by MD).

In the process of onboarding another major overseas semiconductor customer (one of the world's largest manufacturers) with a contract expected to be signed soon, plus additional customers in the space segment this financial year.
open.promised: 1 new large semiconductor customer contract count

open.item: With the DPL license and AS9110 MRO certification in place, MRO is being marketed to existing and new customers in India and the US, with revenue pickup expected in the coming quarters (no number quantified).
open.promised: revenue pickup in coming quarters text

open.item: Revenue mix shifts from the current ~70% aerospace and defence / 30% non-A&D to approximately 50-50 defence versus non-defence next financial year.
With 99% of revenue currently export, the company is targeting Indian PSU and private customers (Tata, L&T, Mahindra) and expects good traction in the short term.
The INR 1,300 crores of cumulative revenue delivered over 14 years (2011 to FY25) will be delivered again within just two financial years, FY26 and FY27 combined.
Profit margins are guided in a 17% to 22% range in the short and medium term, up from the current ~13%.
FY27 growth will be similar to the growth delivered in FY26 (9M FY26 revenue grew 98% YoY to INR 343 crores).
